Ontological Trinity
on-tuh-LOJ-ik-ul TRIN-i-tee
noun phrase (Trinitarian theology)
From Greek ontos (being) + logos (study). The Trinity considered as God is in Himself — the one divine essence subsisting in three co-equal, co-eternal Persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) in their eternal relations. Also called the immanent or essential Trinity. Distinguished from the economic Trinity (the works toward creation).

📖 Biblical Definition

From Greek ontos (being); the Trinity considered as God is in Himself, apart from His works toward creation — the one divine essence subsisting in three co-equal, co-eternal Persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) in their eternal relations. Also called the immanent Trinity or the essential Trinity. The ontological Trinity describes God's eternal inner life: the one undivided divine essence (the three Persons share the one indivisible Godhead, homoousios, of one substance); the three distinct Persons (the Father, the Son, the Holy Spirit, distinguished by their personal properties and relations, not by any division of essence); and the eternal relations of origin (the Father unbegotten; the Son eternally begotten of the Father, eternal generation; the Spirit eternally proceeding from the Father and the Son, eternal procession). The ontological Trinity is the foundation: God is eternally and necessarily triune, independent of creation; He would be triune even if He had never created. The doctrine is grounded in the biblical revelation of the three Persons as fully and equally God (the Father is God, the Son is God, the Spirit is God) yet one God (Deuteronomy 6:4, the LORD is one), and in the eternal relations revealed in Scripture (the Son eternally with the Father, John 1:1; 17:5, 24; the eternal love of the Father for the Son, John 17:24). The Reformed-confessional doctrine (Westminster Confession II.3; the Nicene-Constantinopolitan and Athanasian Creeds) holds the substantive ontological Trinity. The patriarchal-Reformed reader holds the substantive doctrine against the modalist denial (which denies the real distinction of the Persons), the subordinationist and Arian denial (which denies the co-equality and co-eternity of the Persons), and the tritheist error (which divides the one essence into three gods). The ontological Trinity is the eternal reality of the one God who is Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, the foundation of the economic Trinity revealed in the works of salvation.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The Trinity considered as God is in Himself — the one divine essence subsisting in three co-equal, co-eternal Persons in their eternal relations (Father unbegotten, Son eternally begotten, Spirit eternally proceeding); also the immanent/essential Trinity; distinguished from the economic Trinity; God eternally and necessarily triune.

ONTOLOGICAL TRINITY, n. phr. (Trinitarian theology; Greek ontos, being) The Trinity as God is in Himself, apart from His works — the one divine essence subsisting in three co-equal, co-eternal Persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) in their eternal relations. Also the immanent or essential Trinity. The one undivided essence (the Persons homoousios, of one substance); three distinct Persons (distinguished by personal properties and relations, not division of essence); eternal relations of origin (Father unbegotten; Son eternally begotten; Spirit eternally proceeding). God eternally and necessarily triune, independent of creation. Westminster II.3; the Nicene and Athanasian Creeds. Held against modalism, subordinationism/Arianism, and tritheism.

📖 Key Scripture

Deuteronomy 6:4 — "Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD."

John 1:1 — "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God."

John 17:5 — "And now, O Father, glorify thou me with thine own self with the glory which I had with thee before the world was."

Matthew 28:19 — "Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The ontological Trinity is held against modalism (denying the real distinction of Persons), subordinationism/Arianism (denying co-equality and co-eternity), and tritheism (dividing the one essence into three gods); God is one essence in three co-equal, co-eternal Persons.

expand to see more

The ontological Trinity is held against three classic errors. Modalism (Sabellianism) denies the real eternal distinction of the Persons, treating Father, Son, and Spirit as three modes or manifestations of the one God rather than three distinct Persons; this contradicts the biblical revelation of the Persons in real relation to one another (the Father loving the Son, John 17:24; the Son praying to the Father, John 17; the Spirit sent by the Father and the Son). Subordinationism and Arianism deny the co-equality and co-eternity of the Persons, making the Son (and Spirit) lesser or created beings; this contradicts the biblical revelation of the full deity of the Son (John 1:1; 20:28) and the Spirit, and was condemned at Nicaea (the Son homoousios, of one substance with the Father). Tritheism divides the one divine essence into three gods; this contradicts the biblical revelation that the LORD is one (Deuteronomy 6:4). The patriarchal-Reformed reader holds the substantive Nicene-confessional doctrine: one God, one undivided divine essence, subsisting in three co-equal, co-eternal Persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit), distinguished by their eternal relations (the Father unbegotten, the Son eternally begotten, the Spirit eternally proceeding) but not divided in essence. God is eternally and necessarily triune; the ontological Trinity is the eternal reality of the one God revealed in the economy of salvation.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The Trinity as God is in Himself; one essence in three co-equal, co-eternal Persons; eternal relations of origin; Westminster II.3; Nicene and Athanasian Creeds; held against modalism, subordinationism, tritheism.
